cohort: The study included 1241 Japanese city dwellers (521 men, 720 women) aged 41-69 years who underwent medical examinations between 2007 and 2008.
finding: The study found that perinatal conditions such as delivery place, presenting part, and lactation method were associated with higher cardiovascular risk factors in later life among Japanese adults, especially women.
mod_finding: Women born at home exhibited higher HbA1C and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels than those born at the hospital, and men and women born through breech presentation showed higher fasting blood glucose levels than those by cephalic presentation.
